questions.question: Kahn's algorithm finishes and the output order contains fewer nodes than the graph has. What does that mean?
options: The graph contains a directed cycle
Some nodes have no outgoing edges
The queue was implemented with shift()
questions.explanation: Nodes on a cycle always keep at least one incoming edge from another cycle member, so their in-degree never reaches 0 and they are never output.

questions.question: In three-colour DFS cycle detection on a directed graph, which event signals a cycle?
options: Reaching a grey node that is on the current recursion path
questions.explanation: Grey means the node is an ancestor on the current DFS path, so an edge to it closes a cycle. Reaching a black node is just a shared dependency and is fine.

questions.question: For prerequisites given as [course, pre], which direction should the edge go?
options: Direction does not matter for topological sort
questions.explanation: pre must come before course, so the edge points from pre to course and course's in-degree increases. Reversing it silently gives a reversed order.

questions.question: With union by size and path compression, what is the amortised cost of a Union-Find operation?
options: O(log n) worst case per operation, never better
O(α(n)), where α is the inverse Ackermann function: effectively constant
questions.explanation: Combining both optimisations gives O(α(n)) amortised time per operation; α(n) is at most 4 for any realistic n. Without them, find can degrade to O(n).
